note: The words the settings surfaces are made of. Authored here because both platforms say them: a row named one thing in the extension and another on the phone is one product speaking with two voices, and a one-word label is only a choice for somebody who already knows what the other options are. tools/gen_types.py writes them into both.

layer.name: Overlay

about.browser: nothing is replaced; ask about a word yourself
about.phone: nothing is replaced; the button still answers a word

about.browser: the word replaced by what it means
about.phone: the word replaced by what it means

about.browser: the word replaced by how it is said
about.phone: the word replaced by how it is said

about.browser: what it means, and how to say that
about.phone: what it means, and how to say that

layer.note: What a word on the page is replaced by, which is two things and one combination of them - and nothing, for a reader who wants the product there to be asked rather than answering over everything they read.

about.browser: the sounds that tell words apart
about.phone: the sounds that tell words apart

about.browser: every detail of how it is said, like aspiration and devoicing
about.phone: every detail of how it is said, like aspiration and devoicing

dark.name: Light or dark

about.browser: whatever this device is set to
about.phone: whatever this device is set to

about.browser: always the light side of the palette
about.phone: always the light side of the palette

about.browser: always the dark side of the palette
about.phone: always the dark side of the palette

dark.note: Every palette has a light and a dark side. Which one is drawn follows the device unless the reader says otherwise, because a reader who keeps one app light on a dark phone is choosing for a reason.

side.name: Which side

about.phone: for a phone held in the left hand
it stays wherever you put it down
for a phone held in the right hand

side.note: The button sits on this side, and the circle it carries is held away from there, so a hand is never over the word it is on. On neither side it stays where it is left, between the two.

lens-drag.name: Drag it over a word
lens-drag.about: It says what it passes over, and the page under it still scrolls

lens-sweep.name: Hold it, then sweep
lens-sweep.about: Every word it passes over joins the run, and the card answers the whole clause

lens-hold.name: Hold it
lens-hold.about: Turns the overlay off, and on again; the button wears the accent colour while the overlay is on

lens-tap.name: Tap it
lens-tap.about: Ask for the word for something, in the middle of what you are reading; tap it again to put the card away

start.name: Before it can answer a word

touch-words.name: Tap a word for its card

meanings.name: To see what a word means

says.detail-explained: Broad is the sounds that tell words apart; narrow is every detail of how one is said, as a speaker of that accent says it.
says.master-idle: Nothing is drawn over your apps
says.master-unready: Allow it to read the screen and draw over your apps
says.master-working: The words in your apps are being answered
says.no-source: for what a word means; how it is said is built in
says.preview-about: the words on a page this would answer
says.no-direction: No dictionary here for %s, so words cannot be turned into it. The words show how they sound instead.
says.service-stopped: Phonetix is allowed to read the screen but is not running. Switch it off and on again in the phone's accessibility settings.
says.rest-put: Drag the button up or down, or across to the other side.
says.say-no-language: Choose a language to read into first.
says.say-no-model: No translation model for that direction at your dictionary host.
says.start-pack: Get a dictionary for the language you are reading
says.start-permission: Let it read the screen, and draw over it
says.start-target: Choose the language you read into
says.touch-off: Every touch goes to the app underneath, so scrolling is untouched.
says.touch-on: A swipe that starts on a word will not scroll the page.
